clue.text: Misplaced aggression having lost ship from US state

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase, as the answer is when describing someone from there

indicators.note: things misplaced are put in the wrong positions, so the remaining letters get rearranged
having lost something means it has been taken away, so letters leave the word before it

parts.note: taken as written
SS is the standard abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: Some unwelcome hostility, having lost its ship, washes up in an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove SS from AGGRESSION and rearrange the eight letters left to get GEORGIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A person or thing belonging to the American state of Georgia is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Good landlords providing spirits

parts.note: G is the usual abbreviation for good
landlords of pubs host their customers

explanation.surface: Kindly publicans supply the drinks behind the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirits' looks like whisky and gin from the landlords' bar, but it means phantoms.
explanation.definitionFit: Phantoms of the dead that haunt houses are called spirits as well.

clue.text: Bit of work in unusual book

parts.note: odd means strange or unusual
Job is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A small task tucked into a peculiar volume.
explanation.definitionFit: A small piece of casual handiwork, such as a household repair, is a short task of this kind.

clue.text: Talk about line on square vessel

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting on another is placed directly above it
about means going around, so the talk word surrounds the line

parts.note: to gas is to chatter idly
L is the abbreviation for line
S is an abbreviation for square, as in street names

explanation.surface: Someone discusses a line drawn on a square container.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinking tumbler is a vessel, a container for holding liquid.

clue.text: Mischievous line about European sport

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the first two words wrap round the European

parts.note: arch means playfully mischievous, as in an arch look
E is the abbreviation for European
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a railway line

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark is made about a European sporting pursuit.
explanation.walkthrough: Arch here is the adjective for knowing, playful mischief, and RY for line is a railway abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooting arrows at a target with a bow is a competitive sport practised at Olympic level.

clue.text: Place with malaria and other infestation

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in addresses
ague is the old name for malarial fever

explanation.surface: A spot riddled with malaria and other pests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And other' tells us the answer is another affliction alongside malaria.
explanation.definitionFit: A plague of rats or locusts is a large swarm overrunning an area, an infestation.

clue.text: Strange thing swallowed by fish in a flash

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase; the answer is used as an adjective meaning extremely fast

indicators.note: something swallowed ends up inside, so it goes within the fish

parts.note: the ling is a long sea fish of the cod family

indicators.note: something strange is out of its normal form, so the letters of the word after it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd object gulped down by a fish in an instant.
explanation.walkthrough: The ling is a fish solvers meet often; the rearranged letters sit just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done at lightning speed happens almost instantly, like the speed of an electrical storm's bolt.

clue.text: Stop transfer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a colloquial command to cease doing something
second meaning: hand something across to another

explanation.walkthrough: Two words, each a meaning of the same phrasal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a British colloquial way of telling someone to quit, and also means handing control to someone.

clue.text: Simplicity of each essentially delusional head

parts.note: EA is the abbreviation for each

indicators.note: the essence of a word lies at its core, so only its central letters are kept

parts.note: the two central letters of this ten-letter word
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: The simple-mindedness of every deluded mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Being easy or free from difficulty is the quality of simplicity.

clue.text: Munitions regulation one dropped

indicators.note: something dropped is let go, so that letter leaves the word

parts.note: an ordinance is an official rule or decree
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A rule on weapons is abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the I out of ORDINANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Military weapons, ammunition and artillery supplies are collectively termed ordnance.

clue.text: Plants adult donated to society

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for adult, as in film ratings
to donate is to give
S is the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: A grown-up gave some plants to a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plants' looks like a verb about planting something, but it is a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Agaves are succulent plants of the Americas, the source of tequila and sisal.

clue.text: Ran round bend turning up for fight

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading the letters from bottom to top
round means encircling, so the ran word goes around the bend

parts.note: to run a company is to lead it, so ran gives led
a U-bend is shaped like the letter

explanation.surface: Someone hurtles round a corner showing up for a scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal combat between two people, traditionally with pistols or swords, is a fight.

clue.text: Sue tours around about America finding stuff for wedding

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round America
letters sent around are moved about, so the first two words get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
A is an abbreviation for America

explanation.surface: Sue travels across America shopping for things for her wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: SUE TOURS is rearranged into TROUSSEU, with A slipped in before the last U.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride's collection of clothes and linen gathered for her marriage is called a trousseau.

clue.text: Spike in two minds about Henry

indicators.note: about means going round, so the in two minds word surrounds Henry

parts.note: torn means undecided between two options
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A spike of indecision about a man named Henry.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp pointed growth on a rose stem is a spike.

clue.text: Note date with unknown noblewoman

parts.note: la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale
D is the abbreviation for date
Y is a mathematical unknown, like X

explanation.surface: Jot down a date with a mysterious aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like a verb meaning write down; it is the musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman of noble rank, or a peer's wife, is given this title.

clue.text: Destroy nasty coat whatever the consequences

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken apart, so the letters of the next two words are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Get rid of that horrible jacket no matter what.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means regardless of the price or risk involved, no matter what happens.

clue.text: Some exploit ertswhile lags

indicators.note: some means only part of what follows, so the outer letters of the words after it are discarded

parts.note: taken as written; its first three letters are dropped
a misprint for erstwhile, whose opening three letters are kept

explanation.surface: Some former convicts are taking advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a hidden word in 'exploit erstwhile', but the published clue misprints erstwhile, so the stray T must be ignored. Lags is British slang for convicts; here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To lag is to fall behind or dawdle, which is what someone who hangs about idly does.

clue.text: Oddly such mob goes to game

indicators.note: oddly means the first, third and further odd-numbered letters are kept

parts.note: the first and third letters of the word
a rabble is a disorderly crowd or mob

explanation.surface: A rowdy crowd heads off to a match.
explanation.definitionFit: A board game in which players build crossing words from lettered tiles.

clue.text: Sir sent out to embrace Penny — she's single

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold within the arms, so the rearranged letters surround penny
out suggests the letters are knocked out of order and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
P is the abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: A knight is dispatched to hug Penny, who is unattached.
explanation.walkthrough: SIR SENT is rearranged as SINSTER, and P goes in after the first S.
explanation.definitionFit: An unmarried woman, especially an older one, is traditionally described with this word.

clue.text: Head of costumes fitting first class number for lead

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
apt means suitable or fitting
A1 means first-class, written with I for the digit
N is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: The wardrobe supervisor fits a top-quality outfit for the leading actor.
explanation.definitionFit: To captain a team is to lead it, being its chief and commander.

clue.text: Bit of body on a pedestal displayed

indicators.note: displayed means openly on show, here within the words that precede it

parts.note: the letters run across the first three words

explanation.surface: A part of a sculpture is shown off on a plinth.
explanation.definitionFit: The back of the neck is a part of the human body.

clue.text: Playgoer regularly lost attendant

indicators.note: every other letter is regularly removed, keeping the alternate ones

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A theatregoer keeps losing their usher.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy servant or a young helper at a wedding or court is an attendant.

clue.text: A turnip prepared for zealot

indicators.note: vegetables prepared for cooking are chopped up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A root vegetable is made ready for a fanatic's dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A strict moralist with extreme views on religion or behaviour is a zealot of this type.

clue.text: Branded container in part of garden

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the container goes within the garden part

parts.note: a flower bed is part of a garden
an urn is a vase-like container

explanation.surface: A labelled pot sits in a garden plot.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattle are branded by marking their hide with a hot iron, which singes it.

clue.text: Practised poetry with head of department

parts.note: verse is poetry

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A department head who rehearses poems.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well versed in a subject is experienced and skilled in it.

clue.text: 5 is negative with whichever case

definitions.note: a cross-reference to the answer at 5, read as a verb

indicators.note: a case holds something inside it, so whichever wraps round the negative

parts.note: any means whichever one
no is the negative reply

explanation.surface: A cross-reference says one disease is a negative in any situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' looks like a noun meaning situation, but it tells you one piece encases the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The 5-across answer, read as a verb, means to pester or bother someone persistently.

clue.text: Canopy and air conditioning shed in cut

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the first two pieces go within the cut word

parts.note: to pare is to trim or cut
AC is the abbreviation for air conditioning
a hut is a small shed

explanation.surface: A cover and an air conditioner are dumped in a garden shed after cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like a verb meaning discarded; it is the noun for a hut.
explanation.definitionFit: The fabric dome that opens above a skydiver to slow the fall is its canopy.

clue.text: Head to run and frolic

parts.note: a cape is a headland
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Someone heads off for a jog and a romp.
explanation.definitionFit: To caper is to skip or dance about playfully, which is what frolicking means.

clue.text: Bottom touching knob

parts.note: butt is slang for the backside
on means in contact with

explanation.surface: Someone's backside makes contact with a door handle.
explanation.definitionFit: A small round control you press on a device is a knob or switch.

clue.text: Small hints about final allowances

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the hints word goes round the final word

parts.note: tips are useful hints
the end is the final part

explanation.surface: Little clues about the last payments being made.
explanation.definitionFit: Fixed regular sums paid to clergy or trainees as salary are allowances of this kind.

clue.text: Mistakes published by informant overwhelmed by age

indicators.note: something overwhelmed is engulfed, so the informant ends up inside the age

parts.note: an era is an age or period
a rat is someone who informs on others

explanation.surface: Errors printed by a snitch who is past it.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of printing errors in a book, issued as corrections, is given this Latin plural.

clue.text: Meddled with various untried desserts initially

indicators.note: various suggests a mixed assortment, so the letters are arranged differently

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A cook interfered with an assortment of untested puddings.
explanation.definitionFit: To intrude is to butt in where one is not wanted, which is meddling.
